title: US Sold Euros to Save the Yen, Europe Found Out After
excerpt: The US used euros, not dollars, to prop up the yen, catching the European Central Bank off guard with no clear communication.
content_html:
Darryn Pollock

Thu, August 6, 2026 at 8:38 PM PDT 2 min read

The US Treasury sold euros, not dollars, to help prop up the Japanese yen last week. The European Central Bank only learned about the trade after it had already closed.

Christine Lagarde and Scott Bessent only spoke about the move a day later. However, by then, the New York Federal Reserve had already executed the sale for the US Treasury.

Why Washington Reached for Euros Instead of Dollars

Historically, Western central banks have relied on mutual consultation since World War II. They typically planned currency interventions together in advance.

Washington broke that pattern this time. In contrast, it notified the ECB only after completing the trade.

The choice of euros was deliberate, not accidental. Selling dollars might have signaled a retreat from Bessent's strong-dollar policy, so the Treasury tapped its euro reserves instead.

Some analysts argue the yen carry trade rule no longer holds, adding pressure to defend the currency through other means. Bessent has since addressed the intervention directly in his own yen intervention explanation.

Meanwhile, economists have linked the move to concerns that Japan could sell US Treasuries in response.

Europe Reacts to Being Left Out

Senior ECB officials called the episode a break from decades of coordination. One person close to the discussions called the moment unprecedented.

A Treasury spokesperson defended the decision.

"Decisions regarding the allocation of the Exchange Stabilization Fund are made by the US Treasury, taking into account assessments by the Treasury and the Federal Reserve of market liquidity, valuations and other relevant considerations."

However, a senior Trump administration official pushed back on the criticism. The official said Washington respects the confidentiality of talks with foreign counterparts and contrasted that approach with the ECB's handling of the matter.

Market Fallout and What Comes Next

The intervention pushed the yen from roughly ¥164 to about ¥158 against the dollar. Japanese equities absorbed the shock with only modest losses.

Traders now price in a 44% chance the Bank of Japan raises rates in September. BoJ Governor Kazuo Ueda has flagged rising inflation risks as a reason for caution.

The episode leaves European policymakers wondering whether this was a one-off. It could also preview how the Trump administration handles currency defense with allies going forward.

达林·波洛克

太平洋夏令时间 2026 年 8 月 6 日星期四晚上 8:38 阅读 2 分钟

上周美国财政部出售欧元而不是美元来帮助支撑日元。 欧洲央行是在交易结束后才得知这一消息的。

克里斯蒂娜·拉加德和斯科特·贝森特一天后才谈到这一举措。 然而，此时纽约联储已经执行了对美国财政部的出售。

为什么华盛顿选择欧元而不是美元

从历史上看，自二战以来，西方央行一直依赖相互协商。 他们通常会提前共同计划货币干预。

华盛顿这次打破了这种模式。 相比之下，它只是在完成交易后才通知欧洲央行。

选择欧元是经过深思熟虑的，而不是偶然的。 出售美元可能预示着贝森特强美元政策的退出，因此财政部转而动用欧元储备。

一些分析师认为，日元套利交易规则不再适用，这增加了通过其他方式捍卫日元的压力。 此后，贝森特在他自己的日元干预解释中直接谈到了干预问题。

与此同时，经济学家将此举与日本可能出售美国国债作为回应的担忧联系起来。

欧洲对被排除在外的反应

欧洲央行高级官员称这一事件是数十年协调的中断。 一位了解讨论情况的人士称，这一时刻史无前例。

财政部发言人为这一决定进行了辩护。

“有关外汇稳定基金分配的决定由美国财政部做出，并考虑到财政部和美联储对市场流动性、估值和其他相关因素的评估。”

然而，特朗普政府的一名高级官员反驳了这些批评。 这位官员表示，华盛顿尊重与外国同行会谈的保密性，并将这种做法与欧洲央行处理此事的方式进行了对比。

市场影响及下一步发展

此次干预将日元兑美元汇率从约 164 日元推至约 158 日元。 日本股市吸收了冲击，仅出现小幅下跌。

交易员目前预计日本央行 9 月份加息的可能性为 44%。 日本央行行长上田一夫（Kazuo Ueda）将通胀风险上升视为谨慎的理由。

这一事件让欧洲政策制定者怀疑这是否是一次性事件。 它还可以预览特朗普政府未来如何与盟友一起处理货币防御问题。
